eip_proposals_encrypted_mempool.highlight: Optionality problem factored out of EIP-8184 (Lucid) into a separate EIP to reduce cognitive overhead
EIP-8491 (key publisher priority list) published by Jannik; technically same proposal as prior patch to Lucid, with added rationale
Key publisher priority list addresses probabilistic front-running but not proposer-latency optionality abuse (spam risk remains)

research_and_analysis.highlight: Blind sandwich paper methodology questioned: no null hypothesis baseline; Ethereum findings described as a 'nothing burger'; findings on other chains more damning
Paper may evidence trust violations in private mempools (relay leakage), which indirectly strengthens the encrypted mempool case

cl_spec_pr.highlight: consensus-specs#5403 stalled awaiting CL dev review; DOMAIN_SEALED_TRANSACTION_KEY_TIMELINESS and key publisher suffix are open to-do items needing EIP author input

schedule_and_roadmap.highlight: Encrypted mempool inclusion before I-Star deemed completely unrealistic; realistic target is J-Star at earliest
Post-quantum (Hegota) timeline expected to accelerate significantly; next ACD calls anticipated to be contentious

action_items.action: Update consensus-specs#5403 to reflect EIP-8491 changes (commitments, signature fields, validity check)
Add note to consensus-specs#5403 requesting CL dev input on DOMAIN_SEALED_TRANSACTION_KEY_TIMELINESS

decisions.decision: Optionality problem decoupled from EIP-8184; to be addressed in a separate follow-on EIP
No schedule pressure on encrypted mempool; prototype in background, cadence remains monthly check-ins
